sequence_download_slot_E7D99F9F08D3BC89.harness: Claude Code bounded observations: scratchpad seqprobe.py (Chrome over CDP, cache disabled, worker bypassed, Chrome's Slow 4G preset, which caps the whole link; a page-side sampler every 100 ms records each moment two or more sequences hold a source not yet wholly buffered); the iOS Simulator through xcrun simctl (iOS 26.5, an iPhone 16 Pro Max image; an instrumented test copy reporting to scratchpad rateserve.py, which serves the sequences at 225 KB/s in all, one link shared by every download; Safari quit before each run, each run on a port never used before, and only reports from the page the run opened and the build it served counted; the page scrolled by script: the tour to the principle at 13 s and to each system at 16, 23 and 31 s, the jump straight to CytherCAD at 13 s, as the warm-up begins, then ADII at 24 s and AWC-OS at 31 s); scratchpad stalltest.py
sequence_download_slot_E7D99F9F08D3BC89.finding: A reviewer read in js/film.js that a sequence arriving in view loaded and played independently of the warm-up queue, so downloads could overlap, and that the claim 'one clip at a time' was too broad. On the live build C9EF337977140EDC the probe confirmed it: up to three sequences downloaded at once on a phone that scrolled past two, and two on a desktop with two sequences in view.
sequence_download_slot_E7D99F9F08D3BC89.rule: one sequence downloads at a time (the slot); a sequence arriving in view takes it from a clip warming off screen, which drops its download and goes back in the queue, never from another sequence in view, which it waits behind; a free slot goes first to a sequence in view still waiting, then to the next to warm. The film is outside the queue.
sequence_download_slot_E7D99F9F08D3BC89.not_observed: a physical iPhone (its radio, Low Power Mode, memory and thermal limits); the simulator figures are iOS WebKit's behaviour on this Mac, not a phone's

stuck_download_turn.finding: while this was tested, the stall case S2 failed once on build B69B4ABA03A1B1F2 (never committed): a sequence's second arrival never got the download turn. Media events logged in 17 runs showed why: a clip that arrives in one piece may fire progress and suspend before Chrome has parsed it, buffered still empty, and never again (3 of 68 loads, all in one run), so the turn stayed on a clip already whole; the next arrival dropped that clip and the turn stuck on one in view. The live build E7D99F9F08D3BC89 has the same code. Of 35 loads that completed, a full-buffer progress event was seen in 32; a full-buffer progress or canplaythrough in 35.
